revised_core_hypothesis: The natural-history archive is resilient because multiple imperfect fields and surfaces overlap. Artists, shikarees, a writer, Hodgson, medical collaborators and museum zoologists produced distinct but joinable states. Neither name nor number is inherently stable: copying can corrupt names while preserving numbers, and specimen handling can create number collisions. Reconstructibility therefore depends on relational redundancy rather than identifier purity.
